Question: What is a random thought you are having right now?
Answer: Quora is a great platform for sharing your experiences and thoughts. Most people use it as an alternative to journal writing, where they can express their emotions anonymously. There is no other platform quite like Quora, where you can find so many like-minded people—those who have similar goals, whether yet to be achieved or already accomplished, and those who share similar ethnic backgrounds and are within your own state or country. However, it’s not an ideal platform for making online friends, not because of its messaging interface, but due to the unpredictability of human behavior. Once you gain a few followers and views on Quora, you start receiving messages from people. The fact is, you can get tired of seeing the same messages repeatedly. You start noticing patterns and might even experience déjà vu when you realize you've received similar messages before. Online friendships often lose their charm over time if you can’t meet the person in real life, regardless of gender. In the end, it can become a repetitive cycle where you experiences the same conversation with different people. You end up with all the information about them, and it's difficult to accept that you can't talk to them again. Now what to do with all those information?? So, it might be better to avoid this situation or to accept the emptiness that comes with frequently losing online friends and move on more easily to make another.

Question: How can I get rid of overthinking?
Answer: Overthinking arises only when you're not sure about your decision. Suppose you want to message your old school friend who wasn't polite to you the last time you spoke. Now you start to wonder if sending them a message is a good idea: Will they react badly? Will they be rude again, or will they be like the person who used to sit next to you in class? In this situation, there are only two options: There is no third option. If you're going to do something, be 100% sure about it, not 50% or 60%, but a full 100%. If you choose to do it, accept it entirely; if you choose not to, let it go completely and never dwell on it again. ~ Overthinking happens only when you start considering a third option between yes and no. Question: What is the rudest thing a teacher/professor has said or done to you?
Answer: This incident dates back to February 2022. After the COVID lockdown, I was in my graduation, our classes just started in offline mode. There was a teacher in our college who used to teach us corporate accounting. She was in her mid-20s and very arrogant. One day, the class was going fine, and she was teaching us. I noticed a pattern that she was only solving examples on black board and not any practical questions. At a particular example, the given solution in the book was incorrect. The teacher got confused and started writing every other figure to match the answer. Me: "Ma'am, why are you even looking at the solution given in the book?" Ma'am: "I think there is some error in the question. Just move to the next question. We will do it tomorrow.". (But at this point, her ego was hurt.) After some time, she suddenly said, "Why are you talking in the class?" Me: "I was just discussing the question." Ma'am: "I don't want to listen to anything. Come to the first row." Me: "Ma'am, I'm comfortable here." Ma'am: "I said come to the first row." Now I approached the first row. Me: "Ma'am, there are students sitting on both ends. How am I supposed to enter?" Ma'am: "Just jump over the bench." Me: "Ma'am, I'm not an athlete.". (Whole class starts laughing, but her ego is hurt again.) Now settled, seated in a chilling posture, the class is about to end. Ma'am: "You know, I have never met any student like you in my teaching career of 3 years." Me: "Ma'am, but what have I done?" Ma'am: "See, that's the problem. You are not even recognizing your mistake". Frontbechers sitting next to me: "Siddharth, say sorry to ma'am." Me: "But why? What is my mistake?" Ma'am: "You know, students like you don't deserve to be in this college." Me: "I don't want your suggestion." Ma'am: "You don't know how to behave in class and talk to teachers." Me: "I haven't asked for your opinion." Ma'am: "I don't want students like you. Don't ever again come to my class." Me: "Okay, I have no problem." After the class ends, everybody leaves the classrooms. I approached to her. (she in a hope I will apologize to her) Me: "Ma'am, as you said, don't come to my class. Ma'am: "See, I never said you cannot come to my class. But please behave yourself" Me: "Okay, thank you, ma'am." (I thought the matter was resolved.) In the end of the semester, she gave only 10 marks out of 25 in internals 🥲. Her revenge was complete. ~ Siddharth Xyz

Question: What is your most unpopular opinion about people?
Answer: I have heard many times people saying the 90s time period is the golden period; there is pure nostalgia at that time, everything is great back then, people are honest ,friendship are true, there was no social media. And they say all these things after listening to 90's songs or watching movies based on retro themes. There is nothing wrong with that, and obviously, they are correct, but only to an extent. As per me, even if they got a chance to live in the 90s, they would start saying the same thing about the present time period. Now you may wonder why? Because if you start living in the 90s, the first 1-2 months will fascinate you since you are looking at things you only heard about and saw in movies. You're getting a chance to roam around various places and experience new things every other day. But soon after, you get used to that time period, and the 90s, which was a golden age according to you, now becomes your present. Now, you start to see various flaws in this period, like: - For making a call, you have to go to an STD booth. - For watching a movie, you have to wait until it's telecasted on TV. - For listening to a song, you have to wait on the radio for a long time—not like today, where you can hear any song anytime on mobile. - For finding a place, you have to ask every other person on the road. - For traveling on daily basis to college or school, you only have buses; there are no metros. - Frequent power cuts are there. After spending a significant time there and facing all these things, you start missing the present time period. Now you start thinking about the privileges you have in the future and wish to go to the future (i.e., 2023). It's a never-ending process, a kind of vicious cycle. ~Moral of the story is always appreciate what you have got in your life .💫 Siddharth Xyz

Question: What do you know about Lonar Lake of Maharashtra?
Answer: Around 500 kilometres away from Mumbai in the Buldana district of Maharashtra there is a crater which is about 1.8 km in diameter, which was approximately formed around 50,000 years ago when a meteoroid couldn't burn completely and didn't become a shooting star,i.e., meteor and fell here. If you visit that spot now you will see a lake over there Lonar crater Lake. The speciality of this lake is that it's a crater lake. In Order to understand crater Lake, we first need to know about meteoroids. Meteoroids are Rocky object which get separated from comets or asteroids, on entering Earth's atmosphere due to friction these meteoroids heat up and catch fire those who couldn't burn completely become meteorite. They are very rare on earth and one of them is in Maharashtra. In 1823, this crater was identified by British officer CJE Alexander as a unique geographical site. Lonar crater is in the Deccan plateau. since it is located in basalt field it was first thought as a volcanic crater. Uniqueness about lake 1.Ecosystem :-Lonar lake is quite different lunar creator is around 150 m Deep and extremely rare microorganisms are also found here like Gammaproteobacteria, Actinobacteria, Alphaproteobacteria and Betaproteobacteria phyla. 2.Water combination:— The another fact about this lake is that it has both saline and alkaline water in it which is rarely found together. 3.Turned pink:- Months ago the lake is in spotlight of both media and scientists because the colour of the lake turned pink after research it is found it happened because of microbes called Haloarchea which produce pink pigment. 4.Moon minerals:- Study from IIT Bombay has revealed that lunar creators minerals are similar to the moon Rock minerals anorthite, maskelynite albite and zeolite minerals, which are also found in moon rocks brought during the Apollo program. (Maskelynite~ moon mineral) 5.Refrence in Ramayana:— The Lonar Crater Lake, with the lake at its centre, has also been associated with Indian mythology. It has a reference as Panchapsar in the Valmiki Ramayan and has been later written about by the epic poet Kalidas, around 16 centuries ago. He had termed it as the lake Panchapsar in his famous text titled 'Raghuvansh'. (Daitya Sudan temple ~lonar lake) 😉✌️.

Question: How good is Gurgaon as a place to live and settle?
Answer: Gurugram has a lot of things- start ups, hotels, skyscrappers, huge offices. But were it lacks is in- urban planning. And it lacks pretty bad! Cause local Gurugram residents face a lot of issues that are not talked about as much. There are various reason for it — In 2014, 1/3rd people didn't have piped water. Those who had it didn't get proper water supply. In many localities there wasn't water for 3 days due to which 70% of the residents have to depend on groundwater. Results in declining groundwater rapidly. In Gurugram ground water extraction is at massive rate of 300% in comparison to Faridabad at 75%. Water tankers are not afraid affordable which can even cost rupees 1600 per tank. 2. Transport is a problem. There is lack of public transport in Gurugram. There are only 37 bus routes in Gurugram even Mumbai has 370+ bus routes with same land area. Due to which Dependency on cabs and auto increases and they charge high fare prices for it also they become unsafe at night especially for womens. 3. Just 23% electricity is for residents. Massive chunk of electricity produced is consumed by industries. In Gurugram industries consume 45% of the electricity produced and commercial parks consume 32% only a small percentage is left for residents which results in frequent power cuts. 4. 2/3 of the Gurugram is not connected to a sewage system. Because Two third of its area not connected to sewer line disposing waste is a massive problem for residents as well as industries. A lot of filth has to be disposed in reverse and land because of which sanitation becomes a big issue. 5. One of the World's most polluted city. In 2018, It was the world most polluted City. The situation is so bad that since past 10 years people are consuming double limit of PM 2.5 as per WHO standards. In Gurugram one third of the people own private vehicles which is highest in India and these vehicle contributes to pollution. Even rapid construction in gurugram contributes to pollution. 6. Only 3% area covered with greenery. Government is busy in developing a concrete jungle and forgets about giving some importance to environment because of which you can only see building and more building here and empty grounds waiting to be acquired by developers. (Gurugram metropolitan development authority plan) 7. Bad road conditions. Plans to build Road have not been completed. The built roads are not repaired . There are no proper traffic signs, Street lights, zebra crossing, footpath and cycle tracks on the roads. Due to which many accidents occur here. in 2022 these roads have been witnessed one death everyday. Dwarka expressway costing 900 crores was planned in 2006 to connect Gurugram and Dwarka but this project schedule is running behind a decade, Many of you not even heard about this project. There are even more problems but that's it for this answer. So, If you are thinking of buying a home in Gurugram think twice. Thank you for reading :-)
